newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Paynter anticipates 2nd half year loss. [CORRECTED 23:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Paynter anticipates 2nd half year loss. [CORRECTED 23:05 GMT]

text.p: Paynter Timber Group Ltd said on Tuesday it expected a second half year loss to the order of NZ$500,000.
The company earlier reported a first half net profit of NZ$40,000, compared to a loss of NZ$3.88 million in the corresponding period last year.

(Corrects result for previous period from profit to loss). The directors said the modest profit was achieved despite considerable interruptions and lost production during the period as a result of the extensive reorganisation of the company's Hornby manufacturing operation.
An upturn in rimu sawn timber and remanufactured goods turnover created an offsetting benefit for the period.
This was largely responsible for the increase in turnover to NZ$16.3 million from $11.3 million in the latest half year, in an atmosphere of otherwise flat economic activity and housing starts.
The directors had earlier predicted the company would achieve a modest profit for the year to February 28, 1997.
"It is now clear that the cost of the refocusing of the manufacturing business and the disruption to production is such that the company will not achieve that objective," Paynter directors said.

They said lower volume throughput coincided with the traditionally lower sales period, and although the main manufacturing process changes have been achieved, the programme for returning to full production had taken longer than expected.

The directors said they remained satisfied fundamental changes in the company's structure will create the long term benefit sought. Barring significant changes in economic circumstances, they were confident Paynter would return to profitability in the 1997/98 year.
